title: BASL rejects government MP’s claims, challenges MP to repeat allegations outside Parliament - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) today strongly rejected allegations made in Parliament by Government MP Asitha Niroshana Egoda Withanage against BASL President Rajeev Amarasuriya, describing the claims as “utterly false, baseless, and made with malicious intent.”

National People’s Power (NPP) MP Asitha Niroshana Egoda Withanage, speaking in Parliament today, claimed that BASL President Rajeev Amarasuriya had held discussions with Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa, who had allegedly promised him the Western Province Chief Ministerial candidacy at the upcoming Provincial Council election in exchange for his support.

The BASL challenged MP Asitha Niroshana Egoda Withanage to repeat the allegations outside Parliament without the protection of parliamentary privilege, stating that doing so would enable the appropriate legal consequences to follow.

Issuing a statement, the BASL expressed “deep dismay” over what it described as false utterances made under parliamentary privilege and accused the MP of attempting to mislead the public through unfounded and defamatory allegations.

The BASL further expressed concern over what it termed the abuse of parliamentary privilege, stating that such remarks sought to misguide the public and undermine confidence in the legal profession. It also maintained that “cheap political attacks” on the BASL would not succeed, adding that Sri Lanka’s legal fraternity remains united in defending its independence and integrity.

The BASL statement was signed by its Deputy President, President’s Counsel Rienzie Arsecularatne, and Secretary Nalin De Silva.

title: No visa fee change for Sri Lankan pilgrims, India clarifies - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
The High Commission of India in Colombo has clarified that there has been no change in the visa fee policy for Sri Lankan pilgrims travelling to India, while announcing the reintroduction of the free (Gratis) visa facility for eligible pilgrimage groups.

In a statement issued today (24), the High Commission said it remains committed to ensuring the timely and smooth issuance of visas to all Sri Lankan citizens, noting that Sri Lanka is among the countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for India’s e-visa facility.

It stated that Sri Lankans who choose to apply through the High Commission are required to submit their applications online and lodge them at Indian Consular Application Centres (ICAC), located in Colombo, Kandy, Jaffna, Hambantota and Batticaloa.

Addressing concerns regarding visas for pilgrims, including those visiting Buddhist religious sites in India, the High Commission said such visas are facilitated and issued swiftly.

It said that where applications are recommended by the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs, free visas are issued for groups of 10 or more pilgrims.

However, this practice was temporarily discontinued due to a change in the visa outsourcing agency handling applications for the High Commission.

“Subsequent to the selection of the new service provider, which has started working from 07 July 2026, the practice of issuing Gratis visas for Sri Lankans on pilgrimage is being reintroduced,” the statement said.

The High Commission added that pilgrimage visa requests should continue to be forwarded through the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs, and applications can be submitted as groups of 10 or more.

Applicants are required to visit ICAC either as a group or individually for biometric collection, as mandated under new regulations introduced by the Government of India. However, biometric registration is only required for applicants between the ages of 12 and 70.

The High Commission also said a special expedited process has been introduced for senior citizens visiting ICAC for biometric procedures to minimise waiting times.

“Capturing biometrics will ensure that their passage through Indian Immigration on arrival in India is smooth and convenient,” it said.

Clarifying further, the High Commission said there is no visa fee applicable for Sri Lankan pilgrims whose applications are submitted through the prescribed procedure.

However, applicants are required to pay a visa service fee of Rs. 1,855 to the Indian Consular Application Centres for processing services.

title: Rear Admiral Buddhika Liyanagamage assumes duties as Eastern Naval Area Commander - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Rear Admiral Buddhika Liyanagamage formally assumed duties as the Commander of the Eastern Naval Area today (24), at the Eastern Naval Command Headquarters in Trincomalee.

In accordance with naval traditions, the newly appointed Area Commander was received at the Eastern Naval Command before formally taking over his duties and responsibilities from his predecessor, Rear Admiral Kosala Warnakulasooriya.

Rear Admiral Liyanagamage will continue to serve as the Deputy Chief of Staff of the Sri Lanka Navy in addition to his new appointment.

title: 10 killed, including security personnel, in suicide bombing in Pakistan - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Reuters - Islamist militants rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into a Pakistani security checkpoint, killing 15 people, including ‌12 soldiers, in northwest Pakistan, the military said on Friday, adding that 12 militants had been killed in retaliation.

The attack on the post jointly manned by the military and police happened overnight between Thursday and Friday in ⁠the Tank district near the Afghan border, an area that has long served as home to Islamist militants.

Militancy has risen sharply in the northwest Pakistan in recent months.

The army engaged the militants, who after failing to breach the security of the checkpoint drove the explosive laden vehicle into its outer wall, the military's statement said.

Local Taliban militants, also known as ‌Tehreek-e-Taliban ⁠Pakistan, claimed responsibility for the attack, saying four suicide bombers took part in it, according to a statement.

The Taliban have been waging a war against the Pakistani state since 2007 in an ⁠attempt to overthrow the government and replace it with their own brand of strict Islamic governance.

Islamabad says the militants use safe havens ⁠in Afghanistan to train and plan attacks in Pakistan, a charge Kabul denies. Afghanistan says the militancy is Pakistan's ⁠domestic problem.

title: Supermarket fined Rs. 500,000 for selling Nadu rice above controlled price - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - A supermarket in Gampola has been fined Rs. 500,000 after pleading guilty to selling locally produced Nadu rice above the government-controlled maximum retail price.

According to the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA), the supermarket was found selling Nadu rice at Rs. 240 per kilogram, exceeding the prescribed maximum retail price of Rs. 230 per kilogram, during a raid conducted by CAA officers on June 23.

When the case was taken up before the Gampola Magistrate’s Court, the supermarket admitted to the offence, and the court imposed a fine of Rs. 500,000, the CAA said.

title: Eight mangrove ecosystems in Puttalam to be declared Protected Reserves - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Ministry of Environment has decided to designate eight mangrove ecosystems in the Puttalam District as new protected reserves this year.

Accordingly, the gazette notification declaring the reserves is scheduled to be signed on July 27, in conjunction with the International Day for the Conservation of the Mangrove Ecosystem.

The Ministry said the initiative forms part of the national programme aimed at conserving Sri Lanka’s forest ecosystems for future generations. In line with the government’s environmental policy, a new programme titled “Let the Mangroves Flourish” has also been launched to strengthen the protection and conservation of mangrove ecosystems.

Under the programme, selected mangrove ecosystems across Sri Lanka will be declared protected forest reserves to ensure their long-term conservation.

The Ministry further announced that the declaration of the eight identified mangrove ecosystems as protected reserves will coincide with World Mangrove Day, observed on July 26, 2026.

A total extent of 162.72 hectares will be gazetted as new protected reserves under the initiative, the Ministry added.

title: Four arrested over shooting at Wattala birthday party - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Four suspects, including two women, have been arrested for allegedly aiding and abetting the fatal shooting that occurred in the Palliyawatta area of Kadirana, Wattala.

According to Police Media Spokesman Assistant Superintendent of Police F.U. Wootler, the suspects will be produced before the Fort Magistrate’s Court to obtain detention orders to facilitate further investigations.

He also said that five police teams have been deployed to investigate the shooting.

The incident occurred yesterday (23) when a gunman opened fire at a child’s birthday party in Palliyawatta, Wattala, killing a 39-year-old man.

According to police, the shooting was allegedly aimed at a suspected drug trafficker known as “Kudu Roshan” from Mattakkuliya. However, the gunman is believed to have missed the intended target and fatally shot a 39-year-old bystander who was standing nearby.

title: Spain declares national emergency over wildfires near Madrid and in Avila - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Reuters - The Spanish government on Thursday night declared a national emergency after a series of wildfires threatened communities near Madrid and in the neighbouring province of Avila, forcing more than 10,000 people to evacuate as ‌firefighters struggled to contain the blazes.

The Interior Ministry said the decision was taken because of the simultaneous outbreak of several fires, adverse weather conditions and the need to mobilise extensive resources from different public administrations, increasing the complexity of firefighting and civil protection efforts.

Spain and much of southern Europe face increasingly severe ⁠wildfire seasons that scientists have linked to climate change. Experts say abundant vegetation growth following unusually heavy spring rainfall has dried out in extreme summer heat, creating fuel for rapidly spreading fires.

The regional government of Madrid requested assistance, describing the situation as one of "extreme gravity". It said active fires in Villa del Prado, San Martin de Valdeiglesias and Almorox, in neighbouring Castile-La Mancha, had the potential to advance beyond current extinguishing capacity. It also warned that the wildfire in Burgohondo, Avila, could reach the ‌Madrid ⁠region in the coming hours due to weather conditions.

More than 10,000 people have been evacuated from Villa del Prado, San Martin de Valdeiglesias, Pelayos de la Presa and Aldea del Fresno, according to the regional government.

Under Spain's National Civil Protection System law, the declaration places ⁠the emergency under the direct authority of the interior minister, who is responsible for coordinating the response. Authorities said it was the first such declaration linked to a wildfire.

More than 270 emergency ⁠personnel and 40 ground units have been deployed in the affected areas, alongside several Military Emergency Unit(UME) contingents.

More than 100,000 hectares have burned in Spain so far ⁠this year, roughly equivalent to the country's average annual burned area over the past decade. Thirteen people have died, making 2026 one of the deadliest wildfire seasons in decades.

title: No-confidence motion against Justice Minister defeated - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The no-confidence motion brought against Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara was defeated in Parliament by a majority of 116 votes, with 36 MPs voting in favour and 152 against.

Some MPs were absent at the time of voting. These included members of Tamil parties and some MPs from the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB).

The Daily Mirror reliably learnt that Tamil parties would vote with the opposition in the future if the government fails to hold Provincial Council elections.

However, MP Gejendrakumar Ponnambalam voted in favour of the motion.

title: A/L admission card amendments open online until Aug. 3 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The candidates sitting the 2026 G.C.E. Advanced Level (A/L) Examination can make amendments to their admission cards online until 12.00 midnight on August 3, stressing that the deadline will not be extended, the Examinations Department said.

Department Commissioner General A.K.S. Indika Kumari Liyanage said the 2026 G.C.E. (A/L) Examination will be held from August 10 to September 5 at 2,532 examination centres across the country.

The Department said admission cards of school candidates have been handed over to the respective Zonal Education Offices, and school principals should collect them from the Deputy or Assistant Director of Education in charge of examinations in their zones.

Admission cards of private candidates have been sent by post to their personal addresses.

School candidates requiring amendments to their admission cards should access the Department of Examinations website using the username and password provided to school principals and make the necessary corrections online.

Private candidates can make amendments by visiting the same website and entering their National Identity Card (NIC) number.

The Department emphasized that no further extension will be granted after the August 3 deadline.

Candidates seeking further information may contact the Examinations Department through its hotline 1911, telephone numbers 0112784208 or 0112784537, fax 0112784422, or email gcealexamsl@gmail.com.

title: Early optimism gives way to weaker close at the CSE - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Almas Equities Research

The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) closed lower on Friday as early buying interest gave way to profit-taking in several index-heavy counters, pushing both benchmark indices into negative territory by the end of the session. While the market opened on a positive note with broad-based buying across counters, selling pressure intensified during the latter half of trading, erasing the morning’s gains.

The All Share Price Index (ASPI) declined by 26.63 points (-0.13%) to close at 21,172.74, while the S&P SL20 Index fell 3.31 points (-0.06%) to 5,942.56. Total market turnover amounted to LKR 2.45 billion, with 93.56 million shares changing hands.

Despite the weaker close, investor sentiment remained mixed, with healthy participation observed in selected retail counters. Market activity was largely driven by negotiated transactions, as crossings accounted for LKR 1.67 billion, representing 68% of the day's total turnover.

The Retailing sector emerged as the highest contributor to market turnover, recording LKR 1.04 billion with 38.25 million shares traded. UML.N dominated the sector, generating LKR 1.03 billion in turnover while accounting for 38.15 million shares traded. The largest crossing of the day was also recorded in UML.N, amounting to LKR 1.03 billion involving 38.00 million shares.

Market breadth remained marginally negative, with 118 gainers against 129 decliners, reflecting mild selling pressure across the broader market.

On the positive side, LOLC.N contributed 10.62 points to the ASPI, followed by gains from LOFC.N, MELS.N, CARS.N, and DFCC.N. Meanwhile, HNB.N was the biggest drag on the index, shedding 8.47 points, while CINS.N, GRAN.N, COMB.N, and NDB.N also weighed on overall market performance.

Among notable trades, UML.N attracted significant investor interest, recording the day's highest turnover of LKR 1.03 billion with 38.15 million shares traded, while closing with a 4.82% price gain.

Overall, the market reflected a cautious trading environment, with profit-taking limiting early gains despite healthy retail participation. The high proportion of crossings suggests continued institutional activity, while investors remain selective amid the current market conditions.

title: New Chairman and members appointed to Delimitation Commission - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed M. K. Saman Sri Ratnayake as the new Chairman and a member of the Delimitation Commission.

According to the President’s Media Division (PMD), M. B. Rohana Pushpakumara and K. Thavalingam have been appointed as the other members of the Commission.

The letters of appointment were handed over to the newly appointed officials by Secretary to the President Dr Nandika Sanath Kumanayake at the Presidential Secretariat this afternoon (24).

The appointments were made to fill vacancies that arose following the expiry of the terms of office of the previous members of the Delimitation Commission.

title: Navy seizes over three tonnes of smuggled Kendu leaves off Chilaw - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lanka Navy has seized approximately 3,135 kilograms of smuggled Kendu leaves along with three dinghies during a search operation conducted off Karukapane Beach in Chilaw today (24).

The operation was carried out by SLNS Thambapanni, attached to the Northwestern Naval Command, based on information received regarding a suspicious movement in the area.

During the search, naval personnel inspected three suspicious dinghies found off the Karukapane coastal area and discovered the Kendu leaves packed in 80 sacks.

The Navy suspects that the consignment had been smuggled into the country and that those involved had abandoned the dinghies due to increased surveillance by naval personnel in the area.

The seized Kendu leaves and the three dinghies were handed over to the Chilaw Excise Department Office for further legal action.

title: Ex-Southern Province Chief Secretary arrested over alleged Rs. 16.5M fraud - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested Rannulu Chandrasiri de Zoysa, a former Chief Secretary of the Southern Province, over allegations of financial corruption and procurement irregularities.

According to CIABOC, the allegations relate to a project launched in 2019 by the Southern Development Authority, operating under the Southern Provincial Chief Ministry, to provide chairs to voluntary public organisations across the Southern Province. The project was funded through an allocation of Rs. 16.5 million from the Southern Provincial Council.

Investigators allege that the former Chief Secretary had bypassed standard government procurement procedures to select a specific manufacturing company for the project.

CIABOC stated that by favouring the company, de Zoysa had allegedly provided an unlawful financial benefit to the entity, causing a financial loss to the State.

The suspect is scheduled to be produced before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court.

title: Bangladesh’s President Shahabuddin, 76, resigns citing health concerns - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
THE STRAITS TIMES - Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin, a former ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has resigned citing serious health issues, his office said on Friday.

Shahabuddin, 76, has held the largely ceremonial post of president since April 2023, a period that included volatile months after Hasina's flight to India following a student-led uprising against her rule in 2024.

"Recent medical examinations have diagnosed me with a condition known as Autonomic Neuropathy. Due to this condition, I occasionally experience momentary loss of consciousness," Shahabuddin said in a statement released by his press secretary.

The resignation of Shahabuddin would leave Hasina with no allies in high office five months before her planned return. Her Awami League party is banned, and many of its leaders and activists have been jailed or gone into hiding since a deadly student-led uprising toppled her government in 2024.

The speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad, the national parliament, will perform the duties of the president until a new one is elected, the statement said.

As head of state, Shahabuddin is commander-in-chief of the armed forces, but executive power rests with the prime minister and cabinet of the mainly Muslim country of 173 million people.

Reuters reported on Thursday that Shahabuddin, a former ally of ousted premier Sheikh Hasina, would resign on Friday. REUTERS
